page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 128 dedicated virtual CPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced resource ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 32 Gbps.

The instance includes no local storage drives and no discrete GPUs, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data retention and operating system hosting. The hardware architecture utilizes fully dedicated CPU allocations, providing reliable compute capacity without shared core contention. The combination of 128 vCPUs and 32 Gbps network throughput allows substantial network and compute parallelism within a single host node.

From a hardware resource perspective, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating large workloads into a high-density compute node, reducing the need for distributed host management. Without bundled local SSDs or hardware accelerators, allocation is focused on host memory and processor capacity. Appropriate workloads include microservice clusters, large-scale CI/CD build pipelines, enterprise web applications, and database engines attached to cloud block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at 2.6 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it offers 128 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server features a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. It contains no local disk storage and no discrete GPUs, depending entirely on external cloud block storage for persistent data requirements. The high density of dedicated CPU cores makes this instance well-suited for high-concurrency enterprise workloads, microservice deployments, large-scale software compilation pipelines, and container orchestrators requiring balanced compute and memory allocation across a unified node.
